title: Quiet duration
rationale: A large editable duration and one Start action. A single summary row opens mode and pause settings; list management stays outside the session task.
strength: Lowest everyday cognitive load without concealing the chosen rules.
tradeoff: Duration presets are deliberately absent; changing time uses the numeric field.

title: Native menu
rationale: Uses the familiar checkmark menu model. Choosing a duration is a radio-like row, with one explicit Start command below the group.
strength: Compact, keyboard-friendly hierarchy and almost no outlined button chrome.
tradeoff: The whole surface feels like a command menu; long-running status has less breathing room.

title: Timer dial
rationale: The timer is the main object in both setup and active states. A slider changes duration; a quiet ring previews the same geometry used for countdown.
strength: Setup and running states feel like the same object, with very little visual switching.
tradeoff: The ring consumes space and exact unusual durations require Options.

title: A simple sentence
rationale: Presents intent as a readable sentence: Focus for 25 minutes, blocking Distractions. Only the values are editable.
strength: The relationship between time, rules and commitment is immediately legible.
tradeoff: Sentence wrapping is sensitive to longer translated names and larger type.

title: Duration inspector
rationale: Treats the last-used session as a ready-to-run object. Duration, block list and policy are one inspection row, with editing revealed only on demand.
strength: Very calm for repeat sessions; a user can start without reconsidering every setting.
tradeoff: Changing a duration costs one extra click and the summary needs disciplined copy.

title: Until later
rationale: Uses an end time as the central decision and a short time band as its direct manipulation control. Session details are secondary.
strength: Fits work that naturally ends at the next meeting or break.
tradeoff: End-time reasoning can be less intuitive than a familiar 25-minute session.

title: Two decisions
rationale: A small guided sequence separates choosing time from reviewing commitment. Once configured, the active panel stays sparse.
strength: Clear first-use flow with focused decisions and a review before locking.
tradeoff: Repeated sessions take more steps than a direct start; best only for onboarding.

title: Remembered rhythm
rationale: Two named, editable session recipes replace a full setup form. Selecting a recipe sets duration and policy; one Start action runs it.
strength: Fast when someone repeats two distinct routines, such as a short reset and deep work.
tradeoff: Introduces a new recipe concept and will feel excessive for people who use one configuration.
